epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; implied expectations are what you must beat. Before calling a bank cheap after a 10% weekly drop, test what return on tangible equity and capital drag the quote already prices in.
epigraph.author: Bank Valuation Discipline

web_blocks.title: Market-Implied Reverse DCF & HTM-Adjusted Tangible Book Value

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $310.68 ($310.53 in the facts ledger), JPMorgan Chase carries an $825.04 billion market cap across 2.66 billion shares [20, 28, 34]. That price reflects a 10.31% weekly drop from $346.19. Shares now trade at 13.03x trailing P/E ($23.84 TTM EPS) and 12.13x forward P/E [20]. On stated book value of $132.30 per share, the stock trades at 2.35x P/B [20]. On Q3 2026 Tangible Book Value Per Share (TBVPS) of $112.64, the multiple stands at 2.76x P/TBV [28].

Headline P/TBV understates true economic leverage unless you inspect the bond footnotes. In Q3 2026, higher Treasury yields widened AOCI losses by $12.13 billion to -$19.82 billion [28]. That hit pulled TBVPS down sequentially from $113.35 in Q2 to $112.64 despite $15.31 billion of quarterly net income [28]. Separately, Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities carry $25.84 billion in unrecorded gross unrealized losses ($39.51 billion across AFS and HTM combined) [28]. Tax-effecting that HTM mark at 24% removes roughly $19.64 billion, or $7.38 per share, reducing current economic TBVPS from $112.64 to $105.26. At $310.68, JPMorgan therefore trades at 2.76x stated TBV and 2.95x HTM-adjusted TBV [28].

web_blocks.the_number: Reconciled 12-month Base Case fair value is $302.75 per share on stated TBV (-2.55% vs. $310.68 CMP) and $284.30 per share on HTM-adjusted TBV (-8.49% vs. CMP), while $310.68 implies 20.06% perpetual ROTCE on stated TBV (21.20% HTM-adjusted).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We enforce the exact Gordon Growth identity P/TBV = (ROTCE − g) / (CoE − g) using CoE = 9.5% and g = 3.5% (denominator 6.0%). Compounding Q3 TBVPS ($112.64) by +7.5% gives $121.10 stated forward TBV, or $113.72 HTM-adjusted ($121.10 − $7.38/sh). Base 18.5% normalized ROTCE yields exactly (18.5% − 3.5%) / (9.5% − 3.5%) = 2.50x P/TBV: 2.50x × $121.10 = $302.75 (12.2x normalized $24.80 FY27E EPS), or 2.50x × $113.72 = $284.30 HTM-adjusted.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Q3 2026 stated TBVPS ($112.64) and HTM-adjusted TBVPS ($105.26 after -$7.38/sh tax-effected Note 9 mark), live close of $310.68, CoE of 9.5%, terminal g of 3.5%, $1.65 quarterly dividend ($6.60 annualized), ~$108.6B FY26 expense guide, August–September 2026 buyback pause, and 5.5% 2028 G-SIB / Basel III CET1 drag.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Case (15.5% ROTCE = 2.00x): $233.00 on $116.50 stressed TBV (-25.00% vs. CMP), or $218.24 on $109.12 HTM-adjusted TBV (-29.75%). Base Case (18.5% ROTCE = 2.50x): $302.75 on $121.10 stated TBV (-2.55%), or $284.30 on $113.72 HTM-adjusted TBV (-8.49%). Bull Case ($126.00 stated / $118.62 HTM-adjusted TBV): 20.5% ROTCE at 9.5% CoE gives 2.83x ($357.00 stated / $336.09 HTM-adj.), while AOCI healing plus peak 22.5% ROTCE (or 8.9% CoE) supports 3.16x = $398.00 stated (+28.11%) / $374.84 HTM-adjusted.
web_blocks.if_off: If zero net buybacks persist through FY2027, stripping ~150–200 bps of annual accretion slows TBVPS growth from +7.5% to ~5.5% ($118.84 stated / $111.46 HTM-adj.), trimming 2.50x Base fair value to $297.10 stated ($278.65 HTM-adj.). Conversely, falling yields healing -$19.82B AOCI and $50B buybacks support $357.00–$398.00; Card NCOs >4.0% or $449.1B NBFI stress push toward $218.24–$233.00.

web_blocks.html: The Reverse DCF output reveals an essential truth about the selloff. At 2.76x stated TBV, the market still prices JPMorgan for 20.06% perpetual ROTCE under a 9.5% cost of equity and 3.5% growth rate. On HTM-adjusted TBV (2.95x), the implied ROTCE rises to 21.20%. Management's own through-the-cycle ROTCE target is 17.0% [4]. At a 9.5% cost of equity and 3.5% growth, a 17.0% ROTCE bank justifies 2.25x TBV, or $253.44 on stated TBVPS ($236.84 on $105.26 HTM-adjusted TBVPS). Even after dropping $35.51 from $346.19 in one week, JPMorgan is not priced like a distressed bank; it is priced above our reconciled 2.50x Base Case.

web_blocks.title: Re-Pricing 2026 Capital, Expense, and Governance Headwinds

web_blocks.html: Our Pass 1 audit uncovered concrete operational drags that lower our normalized ROTCE from 20% to 18.5%—which under the Gordon Growth identity strictly compresses fair P/TBV to 2.50x ($302.75 stated / $284.30 HTM-adjusted). First, management lifted FY2026 adjusted expense guidance to ~$108.6 billion after 9M 2026 opex jumped 13.7% YoY to $81.46 billion [28]. Second, share buybacks paused in August and September ($664 million net Q3 vs. $15.03 billion gross in 1H 2026) as risk-weighted assets expanded $195.8 billion YTD to $2.18 trillion [28, 35]. Slower share retirement removes roughly 150 to 200 basis points of annual EPS and TBVPS accretion. Under a zero-net-buyback stress test, +5.5% organic TBVPS compounding yields $118.84 stated ($111.46 HTM-adjusted), placing 2.50x Base value at $297.10 stated ($278.65 HTM-adjusted).

Third, regulatory capital inflation now sits directly on the calendar. JPMorgan's G-SIB surcharge climbs from 4.5% to 5.5% on January 1, 2028, lifting its minimum CET1 floor from 11.5% to 12.5% [28]. The March 19, 2026 U.S. Basel III Re-Proposal would lift required CET1 by another ~6% on year-end 2025 positions (~4% combined above the 2028 baseline) [28, 32]. Add the ~$24 billion CECL-covered Apple Card commitment ($106.7 billion unfunded lines, $2.30 billion reserve) and the November 17 CFO handoff from Jeremy Barnum to Bregje de Best [28, 29]. Together, those drags keep our Base valuation anchored at 2.50x TBV ($302.75 stated / $284.30 HTM-adjusted) rather than a peak cycle multiple.

web_blocks.caption: JPMorgan Chase vs. U.S. Money-Center Banks & Stage 2 Financial Insurers (Nov 20, 2026 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every major U.S. bank in the November 20 snapshot (JPM, BAC, WFC, C) broke into Stage 4, while JPM's 13.03x P/E and 2.35x P/B still command a sharp premium over BAC (1.20x P/B), WFC (1.49x), and C (0.96x) that leaves shares slightly above our 2.50x Base fair value.

web_blocks.html: Comparing live multiples across the November 20 snapshot puts JPMorgan's valuation in sharp focus [34]. Bank of America trades at 11.22x TTM P/E and 1.20x P/B with 10.73% ROE. Wells Fargo trades at 11.08x P/E and 1.49x P/B with 12.87% ROE. Citigroup trades at 10.79x P/E and 0.96x P/B with 9.06% ROE. All four money-center banks sit in Stage 4 as financials absorb higher long-end yields and regulatory uncertainty. By contrast, property-casualty insurers Chubb (13.01x P/E, 1.94x P/B, 15.48% ROE) and Progressive (11.65x P/E, 3.89x P/B, 33.24% ROE) hold confirmed Stage 2 uptrends. Note that Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are absent from the November 20 live snapshot feed; on prior November 13 cards, Morgan Stanley traded near 14.72x P/E and 2.71x P/B [26].

web_blocks.title: Sum-of-the-Parts Anchor, Rate Sensitivity & Dividend Floor

web_blocks.html: Breaking JPMorgan into operating units confirms why $284.30 to $302.75 represents a rigorous 12-month Base Case. Asset & Wealth Management oversees $5.21 trillion in AUM and $7.90 trillion in client assets at a 45% segment ROE [28]. Applying 15.0x normalized earnings to AWM (~$80B), 12.0x to CIB (~$336B), and 11.5x to CCB (~$176B), plus Corporate Treasury and excess CET1 capital net of AOCI and HTM marks (~$163B to $212B), yields ~$755B to $804B (~$284 to $303 per share). At $310.68, the stock carries a 1.98% trailing dividend yield ($6.15 TTM) and 2.12% forward run-rate yield ($6.60 annualized at $1.65 per quarter) [20, 31]. That 7.67% earnings yield provides long-term compounding support, yet does not offset negative price upside to our 2.50x Base value.

Valuation Upgrade / Downgrade Trigger: A reversal of AOCI losses above -$10B alongside resumed >$5B quarterly buybacks would lift normalized ROTCE and move Base fair value toward $357.00–$398.00; conversely, Card NCOs breaking above 3.75% or Basel III final rules locking CET1 requirements above 13.5% would compress fair value toward our $233.00 stated ($218.24 HTM-adjusted) Bear Case.

book_paragraphs: Once our price-blind business audit confirmed that JPMorgan Chase retains its Compounder Pass moat, we lifted the curtain on the November 20, 2026 market tape. That screen revealed a stark repricing: in a single week, JPMorgan shares tumbled 10.31% from $346.19 to $310.68. At $310.68, the bank carries an $825.04 billion market value, a 13.03x trailing P/E on $23.84 TTM EPS, a 12.13x forward P/E, and a 2.35x headline price-to-book ratio on $132.30 book value per share.

Yet for a bank, headline book value is only the opening bid. The cleaner gauge is Tangible Book Value Per Share, which printed at $112.64 in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Notice that TBVPS actually slipped sequentially from $113.35 in Q2 despite $15.31 billion of quarterly net income. Why? Rising Treasury yields hammered Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income by $12.13 billion in Q3 alone, widening the AOCI deficit to -$19.82 billion. Worse still, JPMorgan holds $25.84 billion in unrecorded Held-to-Maturity gross unrealized bond losses outside both CET1 and TBVPS. Tax-adjusting that HTM overhang at 24% trims $7.38 per share off tangible equity, reducing economic TBVPS to $105.26 and lifting economic P/TBV from 2.76x stated to 2.95x adjusted.

That balance-sheet footnote explains why you cannot blindly call $310.68 cheap just because it fell ten percent. Plug 2.76x P/TBV into a standard Gordon Growth Reverse DCF with a 9.5% cost of equity and 3.5% perpetual growth, and the market is still pricing in a perpetual ROTCE of 20.06% (or 21.20% on HTM-adjusted TBV). Compare that against management's own 17.0% through-the-cycle ROTCE benchmark, which mathematically justifies 2.25x tangible book ($253.44 stated / $236.84 HTM-adjusted) at a 9.5% cost of equity. Even after a steep weekly drop, Wall Street is still paying for elite execution.

When we rebuild our 12-month fair value strictly from the Gordon Growth identity without anchoring to prior targets, four new Pass 1 facts compress normalized ROTCE from 20% to 18.5%: ~$108.6 billion in FY2026 adjusted expenses, the August–September share buyback pause ($664 million net Q3), the 5.5% 2028 G-SIB / March 2026 Basel III capital inflation (~6% CET1 lift) alongside ~$24 billion in Apple Card commitments, and the 2027 CFO handoff to Bregje de Best. Under our formula P/TBV = (ROTCE - g) / (CoE - g), an 18.5% ROTCE at 9.5% CoE and 3.5% terminal growth yields exactly 2.50x P/TBV—putting Base fair value at $302.75 on $121.10 forward stated TBV (-2.55% vs. $310.68) and $284.30 on $113.72 HTM-adjusted forward TBV (-8.49%).

book_subsections.title: Peer Multiples, HTM Adjustment & Zero-Buyback Stress Test
paragraphs: Look across the November 20, 2026 peer table to see how the broader market is treating big U.S. banks. Bank of America trades at 11.22x P/E and 1.20x book value (10.73% ROE); Wells Fargo sits at 11.08x P/E and 1.49x book (12.87% ROE); Citigroup sits at 10.79x P/E and 0.96x book (9.06% ROE). All four money-center banks broke down into Stage 4 simultaneously as long-end bond marks, capital rules, and macro growth worries weighed on sentiment.

Even at 2.76x stated TBV (2.95x HTM-adjusted), JPMorgan deserves its premium over Bank of America and Citigroup because its 20% reported ROTCE and $5.21 trillion AWM engine sit in a different league. Valuing AWM at 15x normalized profit (~$80B), CIB at 12x (~$336B), and CCB at 11.5x (~$176B) alongside Corporate Treasury net of AOCI/HTM marks yields a Sum-of-the-Parts range of $284 to $303 per share, squarely confirming our 2.50x Base model.

Let us verify all three Gordon Growth scenarios cleanly on both stated and HTM-adjusted TBV. In the Base Case (18.5% ROTCE, 2.50x), stated fair value is $302.75 on $121.10 forward TBV and HTM-adjusted fair value is $284.30 on $113.72. Stress-testing +7.5% TBVPS compounding under zero net buybacks trims growth to ~5.5% ($118.84 stated / $111.46 HTM-adjusted), lowering 2.50x Base value to $297.10 stated ($278.65 HTM-adjusted). In the Bear Case (15.5% ROTCE, 2.00x), stated fair value is $233.00 on $116.50 stressed TBV (-25.00%) and HTM-adjusted fair value is $218.24 on $109.12 (-29.75%). In the Bull Case ($126.00 stated / $118.62 HTM-adjusted TBV), 20.5% ROTCE at 9.5% CoE gives 2.83x ($357.00 stated / $336.09 HTM-adjusted), while AOCI healing and 22.5% peak ROTCE (or 8.9% CoE) support 3.16x ($398.00 stated / $374.84 HTM-adjusted).

Let us also check what dividend support does for long-term owners at $310.68. At a $6.15 trailing dividend ($6.60 annualized run-rate following June 2026's 10% raise to $1.65 per quarter), JPMorgan yields roughly 2.0% to 2.1% while earning a 7.67% trailing earnings yield. That cash payout keeps the bank compounding steadily over a decade, yet it cannot rescue near-term price returns when shares already trade above both $302.75 stated and $284.30 HTM-adjusted Base fair value.

book_subsections.title: Why Strict Gordon Growth Discipline Changes the Entry Math
paragraphs: Notice how enforcing exact valuation arithmetic protects your capital discipline. In our prior November 13 review, a $388.09 Base Case made waiting near $335 look richly asymmetric. Once we price in -$19.82 billion of AOCI marks, -$7.38 per share of HTM bond losses, halted August–September buybacks, a $108.6 billion cost base, and upcoming Basel III capital drag—and strictly enforce 2.50x P/TBV for 18.5% ROTCE at 9.5% CoE—our Base fair value falls to $302.75 stated ($284.30 HTM-adjusted).

That means JPMorgan at $310.68 is not merely trapped in a Stage 4 downtrend; it also trades 2.6% above stated Base fair value and 9.3% above HTM-adjusted Base fair value. Before you jump at a 10% weekly drop, you have to test both the tape and the post-reclaim upside—a test we run on the live chart in Chapter 8.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: At $310.68 (2.76x stated Q3 TBV of $112.64, or 2.95x HTM-adjusted TBV of $105.26), JPMorgan Chase still implies 20.06%–21.20% perpetual ROTCE. Strictly applying P/TBV = (ROTCE - g) / (CoE - g) at 18.5% ROTCE, 9.5% CoE, and 3.5% g yields 2.50x—setting 12-month Base fair value at $302.75 stated ($284.30 HTM-adjusted).
bullets: Reverse DCF (9.5% CoE, 3.5% g): 2.76x stated P/TBV implies 20.06% ROTCE vs. 17.0% cycle target (2.25x = $253.44 stated / $236.84 HTM-adj.).
